scope: Released Agency documentation and observable CLI behavior

claims.statement: Agency describes its client as a thin integration layer around supported agent engines.
Released Agency entry points include a local CLI, GitHub Copilot App Agency mode, Azure DevOps experiences, and APIs.
Agency discovers configuration from the user-level location through repository and nearer-directory files, with closer files taking precedence.
Remote configuration is merged beneath the local values of the file that declares it, and transitive remote configuration is rejected.
Named profiles can overlay base configuration, while isolated profile activation removes base and ambient host MCP configuration.
Plugins are Agency's primary distribution unit for agents, skills, MCPs, and related resources.
Agency supports ephemeral session plugins and persistent plugins managed through configuration.
Agency custom agents use Markdown with YAML frontmatter and remain compatible with the GitHub Copilot custom agent schema.
MCP tool exposure and agent tool allowlists restrict usable tools, while the backing service credential remains authoritative for authorization.

claims.statement: Plugin evals measure a plugin against authored scenarios, while batch runs measure agent reliability across a dataset.

claims.statement: Plugin-eval grading definitions are withheld from the evaluated agent.

claims.statement: The default plugin-eval harness uses per-task containers, while the host harness provides no malicious-task isolation boundary.
Batch-run iterations measure repeated reliability, while attempts provide retry tolerance within an iteration.

evidence.section: How a batch run is put together

claims.statement: Agency Telemetry provides an access-controlled, privacy-scrubbed selection of activity and outcome events rather than raw transcripts.
Agency readiness guidance prioritizes outcome measures and deterministic validation over file-presence signals.
GitHub Copilot App Agency mode uses the same Agency foundation for configuration and integrations, while app-specific workflows can differ from the CLI.
The Agency API creates, validates, manages, and monitors hosted jobs in Azure DevOps.
Agency Hub in Azure DevOps starts, manages, and monitors background agent work from a browser.
Local Agency sessions load a version-matched built-in Agency plugin that includes support and pull-request completion skills without adding them to user plugin configuration.
The plugin-evaluation command family is documented as experimental and version-sensitive.
Agency marketplace scopes represent different curation and operational maturity levels.
Plugin engine compatibility is explicit and does not imply identical behavior across every supported engine.
Agency is best modeled as an integration, governance, and execution control plane around agent engines.
The product can be taught as six layers: surfaces, Agency control, portable capabilities, engine adapters, tools and resources, and execution environments.
Agency configuration is a provenance-aware merge graph rather than a single linear precedence list.
Effective tool access is the intersection of implemented tools, exposed tools, agent allowlists, and backing-service authorization.
Local sessions and hosted jobs share capability concepts but have distinct identity, configuration, compute, and validation boundaries.
The released improvement loop is observe, encode, evaluate, govern, deploy, and measure again.
Use isolated profiles when a run must not inherit ambient user or editor MCP configuration.
Pin mutable plugin, remote-configuration, artifact, and pipeline inputs when reproducibility matters.
Verify hosted agent results with deterministic checks, tests, policy, artifact inspection, or human review.
Use plugin evals for capability quality, include negative cases, and use batch runs for repeated reliability.
Do not treat installability as proof of trust; consider source, ownership, pinning, review, and marketplace maturity.
Measure telemetry at the entity grain that answers the question and account for delayed and intentionally incomplete coverage.
Test local and hosted behavior separately because policy, identity, network, and compute boundaries differ.
Encode lessons in the strongest practical mechanism: deterministic check, regression test, eval, runtime policy, then guidance.
